controls.title: Network security control governance
controls.description: Keep written policies and procedures for firewalls and similar network controls current, in use, and known to staff, with clear ownership of each related duty.

controls.title: Configure and maintain network controls
controls.description: Set up firewalls, routers, and cloud security groups from approved standards, keep network and data-flow diagrams accurate, justify every allowed service, and review rulesets on a regular cycle.

controls.title: Restrict traffic into and out of the CDE
controls.description: Allow only the specific inbound and outbound traffic the cardholder environment truly needs, deny everything else, and tightly limit traffic between wireless networks and the CDE.

controls.title: Control trusted-to-untrusted network connections
controls.description: Place filtering controls between internal and public networks, keep systems holding card data off directly reachable segments, block spoofed addresses, and avoid exposing internal addressing externally.

controls.title: Protect devices that roam onto untrusted networks
controls.description: Laptops and other endpoints that touch the CDE and also join outside networks such as home Wi-Fi need firewall-style protection that users cannot switch off without authorization.

controls.title: Secure configuration governance
controls.description: Maintain documented, current procedures for hardening systems, communicate them to the people who use them, and assign responsibility for configuration activities.

controls.title: Harden and manage system components
controls.description: Build systems from hardening baselines, change or disable vendor default accounts, run one primary function per server where practical, strip unneeded services, and encrypt administrative access.

controls.title: Secure wireless environments
controls.description: For any Wi-Fi tied to the CDE or carrying card data, replace vendor defaults such as keys and passwords, and rotate keys whenever someone with knowledge of them leaves.

controls.title: Stored data protection governance
controls.description: Document and maintain procedures for safeguarding stored cardholder data, keep them current and in use, and make sure staff know who is responsible for what.

controls.title: Minimize stored account data
controls.description: Keep only the cardholder data the business needs, set retention limits, and securely purge anything past its retention period, checking at least quarterly.

controls.title: Never retain sensitive authentication data
controls.description: Once a transaction is authorized, do not keep full track data, card verification codes, or PINs, even in encrypted form, unless the organization is an issuer with a documented need.

controls.title: Limit PAN display and copying
controls.description: Mask card numbers on screens and reports so only people with a genuine need see more than the first six and last four digits, and block copying of card data through remote access tools.

controls.title: Make stored PAN unreadable
controls.description: Render card numbers unreadable wherever they are kept, using strong one-way hashes, truncation, tokenization, or encryption with sound key management, including on removable media and backups.

controls.title: Protect stored-data encryption keys
controls.description: Keep keys that protect card data away from unauthorized people, store as few copies as possible in as few places as possible, and wrap data-encrypting keys with stronger key-encrypting keys.

controls.title: Key lifecycle management
controls.description: Document and follow a full key management process: generating strong keys, distributing and storing them safely, rotating at end of cryptoperiod, retiring compromised keys, split knowledge, and custodian acknowledgment.

controls.title: Transmission encryption governance
controls.description: Maintain current, documented procedures for encrypting card data sent over networks, keep them in use, and make sure the responsible staff understand them.

controls.title: Encrypt PAN sent over open networks
controls.description: Use trusted certificates and modern protocols such as current TLS when card numbers cross public networks, keep an inventory of those certificates, and never send PAN unprotected via email or chat.

controls.title: Malware defense governance
controls.description: Keep anti-malware policies and procedures documented, up to date, and actually followed, and assign clear ownership for malware protection activities.

controls.title: Prevent and detect malware
controls.description: Run anti-malware software on systems at risk, and for systems judged low-risk, periodically reassess that judgment to confirm they still do not need it.

controls.title: Keep anti-malware active and current
controls.description: Keep anti-malware tools updated, scanning or monitoring continuously, logging their activity, and protected so users cannot turn them off without approval; scan removable media when connected.

controls.title: Defend users against phishing
controls.description: Deploy technical measures, such as email filtering and link protection, that catch phishing messages before they reach staff or limit the damage when they do.

controls.title: Secure development governance
controls.description: Keep documented, current procedures for building and maintaining secure systems and software, ensure they are followed, and assign responsibility for each activity.

controls.title: Build custom software securely
controls.description: Develop in-house and bespoke software using secure coding practices, train developers at least yearly, and review code before release to catch flaws like injection and broken authentication.

controls.title: Find and fix vulnerabilities
controls.description: Track new vulnerabilities from reliable sources, rank them by risk, keep a software and component inventory, and patch critical issues quickly and others within a reasonable window.

controls.title: Protect public-facing web applications
controls.description: Shield internet-facing web apps with an automated attack-blocking solution such as a WAF, and manage and authorize every script running on payment pages in the consumer's browser.

controls.title: Manage changes securely
controls.description: Run changes through a documented process with impact analysis, approval, testing, and rollback plans; keep test and production separate and never use live card numbers in testing.

controls.title: Access restriction governance
controls.description: Document and maintain procedures for limiting access to systems and card data based on business need, keep them current, and assign who owns each duty.

controls.title: Define and assign access by need
controls.description: Grant access using least privilege based on each person's job role, require approval for privileges, review user and application accounts on a regular cycle, and limit database query access.

controls.title: Enforce access through a control system
controls.description: Use an access control mechanism that grants rights by role and need, applies to every system component, and denies everything by default.

controls.title: Identity and authentication governance
controls.description: Keep identification and authentication procedures documented, current, and in use, with clear roles for the people who carry them out.

controls.title: Manage user IDs across their lifecycle
controls.description: Give every person a unique ID, avoid shared or generic accounts, authorize account creation and changes, promptly remove leavers, disable dormant accounts, and limit vendor remote access windows.

controls.title: Strong authentication for users
controls.description: Protect authentication factors in transit and storage, verify identity before resetting credentials, lock out repeated failures, require reasonably long and complex passwords, and change them when compromised.

controls.title: Require MFA for CDE access
controls.description: Require multi-factor authentication for all administrative access into the cardholder environment, for any non-console access to it, and for every remote network connection.

controls.title: Harden MFA against misuse
controls.description: Configure MFA so it resists replay, cannot be bypassed without documented approval, needs at least two distinct factor types, and grants access only after every factor succeeds.

controls.title: Control system and application accounts
controls.description: Limit interactive logins on system and service accounts, keep their passwords out of scripts and config files, and rotate those passwords based on risk.

controls.title: Physical security governance
controls.description: Maintain documented, current procedures for limiting physical access to card data and make sure staff understand their roles in carrying them out.

controls.title: Control entry to sensitive facilities
controls.description: Use badge systems, locks, or cameras to govern entry to sites and rooms holding card data, retain entry records, and restrict network jacks and console access in public areas.

controls.title: Authorize and manage personnel and visitors
controls.description: Make employees and visitors easy to tell apart, approve and escort visitors, issue badges that expire, revoke access promptly when no longer needed, and keep a visitor log.

controls.title: Secure media containing card data
controls.description: Physically secure, classify, and inventory media holding card data, track it when moved off-site, and destroy it so the data cannot be recovered once it is no longer needed.

controls.title: Protect payment terminals from tampering
controls.description: Keep a list of card-reading devices, inspect them regularly for tampering or swapped units, and train staff at the point of sale to spot and report suspicious activity.

controls.title: Logging and monitoring governance
controls.description: Document and maintain logging and monitoring procedures for activity on systems and card data, keep them in use, and assign clear ownership.

controls.title: Capture audit logs of key events
controls.description: Log user access to card data, admin actions, log access, failed logins, account changes, and audit setting changes, recording who, what, when, where, and the outcome.

controls.title: Protect audit logs
controls.description: Restrict read access to logs, prevent unauthorized changes, back them up promptly to a central server, and use integrity monitoring so tampering is noticed.

controls.title: Review logs for suspicious activity
controls.description: Look at security event and critical system logs every day, preferably with automated tools, review other logs at a risk-based interval, and follow up on exceptions.

controls.title: Retain audit log history
controls.description: Keep at least a year of audit log history, with the most recent three months readily accessible for investigation.

controls.title: Synchronize system clocks
controls.description: Use a time-synchronization service so all systems agree on the time, restrict who can change time settings, and get time from trusted sources.

controls.title: Detect security control failures
controls.description: Monitor critical controls such as firewalls, IDS, anti-malware, and logging for failures, raise alerts quickly, and restore them while documenting cause and remediation.

controls.title: Security testing governance
controls.description: Keep documented, current procedures for routinely testing systems and networks, ensure they are followed, and assign responsibility for testing tasks.

controls.title: Find and handle rogue wireless access points
controls.description: Check for wireless access points at least quarterly, keep an inventory of authorized ones, and act on any unauthorized devices discovered.

controls.title: Run internal and external vulnerability scans
controls.description: Scan internal systems and use an approved scanning vendor externally at least every quarter and after major changes, then rescan to confirm high-risk findings are fixed.

controls.title: Perform penetration testing
controls.description: Test networks and applications from inside and outside at least yearly and after big changes using a defined methodology, verify segmentation, and fix exploitable findings.

controls.title: Detect intrusions and unexpected file changes
controls.description: Use intrusion detection or prevention at the CDE perimeter and key points, keep detection engines current, and monitor critical files for unauthorized modifications.

controls.title: Detect tampering on payment pages
controls.description: Watch the payment pages served to customer browsers for unauthorized changes to scripts or security headers and alert staff when something is altered.

controls.title: Information security policy
controls.description: Publish an overall security policy, revisit it at least annually, spell out security roles for all personnel, and give a named executive responsibility for the security program.

controls.title: Acceptable use of end-user technology
controls.description: Set rules for how staff may use laptops, mobile devices, removable media, and similar technology, require management approval, and list permitted products and uses.

controls.title: Identify and manage risks to the CDE
controls.description: Perform targeted risk analyses for flexible requirements, justify any customized approaches, review cryptography and hardware or software in use, and keep these analyses current.

controls.title: Executive ownership of PCI compliance
controls.description: Assign leadership accountability for protecting card data and running the compliance program; service providers also confirm staff perform their assigned tasks through periodic reviews.

controls.title: Document and confirm PCI scope
controls.description: Keep an inventory of in-scope systems, confirm the scope and data flows at least yearly and after major changes, and verify segmentation boundaries remain accurate.

controls.title: Ongoing security awareness training
controls.description: Run a security awareness program covering threats like phishing and social engineering, train staff at hire and at least yearly, and have them acknowledge the policies.

controls.title: Screen personnel before hiring
controls.description: Run background checks, as far as local law permits, on new hires whose role gives them reach into the card data environment, before they begin work.

controls.title: Manage third-party service provider risk
controls.description: Keep a list of service providers that touch card data, get written agreements on their security duties, vet them before engagement, and monitor their compliance status yearly.

controls.title: Service providers support customer compliance
controls.description: Service providers acknowledge in writing their responsibility for card data they handle and give customers the information needed to understand which requirements each party covers.

controls.title: Incident response readiness
controls.description: Maintain and test an incident response plan, have staff available around the clock to respond to alerts, train responders, and act on any card data found where it should not be.
